newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- ends unchanged to up 1/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- ends unchanged to up 1/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were unchanged to up 1/8 point in late trading Thursday, after trading flat much of the day.
Traders said the tone felt firm throughout the session, even through several bid-wanted lists that some traders expected would drag prices lower.
Munis rose with other fixed income markets early in the day after an unexpected rise in new jobless claims, to 347,000, for the week ended June 14.

The markets declined, however, after the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia said its index of business activity in the manufacturing sector rose to 25.2 in June from 1.6 in May. Economists had expected the figure to be just 7.3.
But by late in the session Treasury prices had also returned to positive territory, with the government long bond up 4/32 at 99-10/32, moving the yield down to 6.68 percent.
In the new issue market, Goldman Sachs & Co said it repriced Thursday's largest negotiated deal, a $356 million sale of refunding bonds by the Municipal Assistance Corp. for New York City.
The firm lowered yields in several maturities at the repricing and cut the top yield in 2008 to 4.90 percent from 4.95 percent. To see the repricing scale, double click on nN19281634.

On the competitive side, Prudential Securities won the largest issue, a $23 million Warren County Justice Center Expansion Corp., Ky., deal. Prudential reoffered the 2029 terms at a 5.474 percent yield. To see the reoffering scale, double click on nN1849389.

September municipal futures also returned to positive territory at the close, with September municipal futures ending up 1/32 at 118-11/32. September Treasury bond futures also gained 1/32 to 112-6/32, leaving the MOB spread unchanged from Wednesday at 197 ticks.
In secondary trading, Orange County, Fla., MBIA School Board 5-3/8s Certificates of Participation of 2022 were bid at 5.54 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey FGIC 5-1/2s of 2026 were bid at 99-1/2, up 1/8 from Wednesday.
